Typography.StylisticSet15="False" Typography.StylisticSet16="False" Typography.StylisticSet17="False" Typography.StylisticSet18="False" Typography.StylisticSet19="False" Typography.StandardSwashes="0" Typography.ContextualSwashes="0" Typography.StylisticAlternates="0"> <Paragraph><Run>When software requests DFU to update to the target firmware, the target firmware will expect software to acknowledge the update to confirm that the new firmware is able to successfully communicate. If the acknowledgement doesn't arrive within this timeout period (starting from the time that the target firmware starts up), the firmware will automatically fall back to the previous firmware.</Run></Paragraph> </Section>

Parameter.name: FirmwareUpdateRestrictedClientEnable
Parameter.Description: Restricted client enable. If true and ManagedSingleClientEnable is true, then only the wireless Piccolo client that initiated the DFU will be permitted to reconnect during the DFU acknowledgement phase.
Parameter.EngineeringNote: <Section xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation" xml:space="preserve" TextAlignment="Left" LineHeight="Auto" IsHyphenationEnabled="False" Typography.StylisticSet4="False" Typography.StylisticSet5="False" Typography.StylisticSet6="False" Typography.StylisticSet7="False" Typography.StylisticSet8="False" Typography.StylisticSet9="False" Typography.StylisticSet10="False" Typography.StylisticSet11="False" Typography.StylisticSet12="False" Typography.StylisticSet13="False" Typography.StylisticSet14="False" Typography.StylisticSet15="False" Typography.StylisticSet16="False" Typography.StylisticSet17="False" Typography.StylisticSet18="False" Typography.StylisticSet19="False" Typography.StylisticSet20="False" Typography.Fraction="Normal" Typography.SlashedZero="False" Typography.MathematicalGreek="False" Typography.EastAsianExpertForms="False" Typography.Variants="Normal" Typography.Capitals="Normal" Typography.NumeralStyle="Normal" Typography.NumeralAlignment="Normal" Typography.EastAsianWidths="Normal" Typography.EastAsianLanguage="Normal" Typography.StandardSwashes="0" Typography.ContextualSwashes="0" Typography.StylisticAlternates="0"> <Paragraph><Run>This parameter is intended to be used to prevent the wrong Piccolo client reconnecting to the aid during the firmware update phase of DFU. If the wrong client connects it will be unaware that the firmware needs an acknowledgment from the client to finalize the DFU, the firmware will then timeout and revert back to the old firmware.</Run></Paragraph> <Paragraph><Run>This parameter only has an effect in managed single client mode, i.e. when ManagedSingleClientEnable is true. In managed multi-client mode it doesn't matter if another client reconnects first because the originating client will still be allowed to connect and complete the DFU.</Run></Paragraph> <Paragraph><Run>The "correct" client is identified by the client's bond key handle and therefore this check relies on two things being true:</Run></Paragraph> <List MarkerStyle="Decimal"> <ListItem> <Paragraph><Run>The bond key file is preserved as part of the DFU preservation script</Run></Paragraph> </ListItem> <ListItem> <Paragraph><Run>There are no changes to the way that bond key handles are associated with bonds</Run></Paragraph> </ListItem> </List> <Paragraph><Run>Because these statements might not be true, this parameter is expected to default to false to prevent DFU failing. Software can set it to true at some point before a DFU and preserve it in the preservation script or explicitly set it to true in the preservation script.</Run></Paragraph> </Section>

Parameter.name: FitType

Parameter.name: ManagedSingleClientEnable
Parameter.Description: Managed single client mode enable. If true, then only one wireless Piccolo client is permitted to communicate with the aid at any one time.

Typography.StandardSwashes="0" Typography.ContextualSwashes="0" Typography.StylisticAlternates="0"> <Paragraph><Run>When set to false, the wireless interface operates in managed multi-client mode. This allows multiple BLE devices to connect to the aid and multiple applications on a single device to have independent Piccolo interfaces. If the maximum number of interfaces supported by the aid is exceeded, the client will receive a a DevServiceUnavailable ENS message with the reason code set to InsufficientResources.</Run></Paragraph> <Paragraph><Run>When set to true, the wireless interface operates in managed single client mode. This permits only a single application on a single BLE device to establish a Piccolo interface. In this mode, a client that is denied will receive a DevServiceUnavailable ENS message with the reason code set to ManagedSingleClient.</Run></Paragraph> </Section>

ParameterGroup.name: PowerManagementChargingConfiguration
ParameterGroup.Description: Power management integrated circuit (PMIC) charging configuration parameters

Parameter.name: ErTmiBatteryDischargeCurrentFullScale
Parameter.Description: Battery discharge full-scale current value
Parameter.EngineeringNote: IMON_DISCHG_SCALE 7:4 Selects the battery discharge current full-scale current value. 0x0 = 8.2mA 0x1 = 40.5mA 0x2 = 72.3mA 0x3 = 103.4mA 0x4 = 134.1mA 0x5 = 164.1mA 0x6 = 193.7mA 0x7 = 222.7mA 0x8 = 251.2mA 0x9 = 279.3mA 0xA to 0xF = 300.0mA

Parameter.name: ErTmiBatteryThermistorEnable
Parameter.Description: Battery thermistor enable (JETIA modified charging)

Parameter.name: ErTmiChargeTopOffTime
Parameter.Description: Time to continue charging battery after termination current reached

Parameter.name: ErTmiChargingEnable
Parameter.Description: Battery charging enable
Parameter.EngineeringNote: CHG_EN 0 Charger Enable 0 = The battery charger is disabled. 1 = The battery charger is enabled.

Parameter.name: ErTmiColdBatteryTemperatureThreshold
Parameter.Description: Battery temperature threhold to enter JEITA cold mode
Parameter.EngineeringNote: THM_COLD 1:0 Sets the V COLD JEITA Temperature Threshold 0b00 = V COLD = 1.024V (-10ºC for β = 3380K) 0b01 = V COLD = 0.976V (-5ºC for β = 3380K) 0b10 = V COLD = 0.923V (0ºC for β = 3380K) 0b11 = V COLD = 0.867V (5ºC for β = 3380K)

Parameter.name: ErTmiCoolBatteryTemperatureThreshold
Parameter.Description: Battery temperature threhold to enter JEITA cool mode
Parameter.EngineeringNote: THM_COOL 3:2 Sets the V COOL JEITA Temperature Threshold 0b00 = V COOL = 0.923V (0ºC for β = 3380K) 0b01 = V COOL = 0.867V (5ºC for β = 3380K) 0b10 = V COOL = 0.807V (10ºC for β = 3380K) 0b11 = V COOL = 0.747V (15ºC for β = 3380K)

Parameter.name: ErTmiFastChargeConstantCurrent
Parameter.Description: Fast-charge constant current value (limited to multiples of 5 mA)
Parameter.EngineeringNote: CHG_CC 7:2 Sets the fast-charge constant current value, I FAST-CHG . This 6-bit configuration is a linear transfer function. For MAX77659A, it starts at 7.5mA and ends at 300mA, with 7.5mA increments. For MAX77659S, it starts at 5.0mA and ends at 200mA, with 5.0mA increments. For MAX77659A: 0x0 = 7.5mA 0x1 = 15.0mA 0x2 = 22.5mA ... 0x26 = 292.5mA 0x27 to 0x3F = 300.0mA For MAX77659S: 0x0 = 5.0mA 0x1 = 10.0mA 0x2 = 15.0mA ... 0x26 = 195.0mA 0x27 to 0x3F = 200.0mA

Parameter.name: ErTmiFastChargeConstantVoltage
Parameter.Description: Fast-charge constant voltage value

Parameter.name: ErTmiFastChargeCoolWarmBatteryConstantCurrent
Parameter.Description: Fast-charge JEITA cool/warm battery constant current value (limited to multiples of 5 mA)
Parameter.EngineeringNote: CHG_CC_JEITA 7:2 Sets I FAST-CHG-JEITA for when the battery is either cool or warm as defined by the V COOL and V WARM temperature thresholds. This register is a don't care if the battery temperature is normal. This 6-bit configuration is a linear transfer function. For MAX77659A, it starts at 7.5mA and ends at 300mA, with 7.5mA increments. For MAX77659S, it starts at 5.0mA and ends at 200mA, with 5.0mA increments. For MAX77659A: 0x0 = 7.5mA 0x1 = 15.0mA 0x2 = 22.5mA ... 0x26 = 292.5mA 0x27 to 0x3F = 300.0mA For MAX77659S: 0x0 = 5.0mA 0x1 = 10.0mA 0x2 = 15.0mA ... 0x26 = 195.0mA 0x27 to 0x3F = 200.0mA

Parameter.name: ErTmiFastChargeCoolWarmBatteryConstantVoltage
Parameter.Description: Fast-charge JEITA cool/warm battery constant voltage value

Parameter.name: ErTmiFastChargeSafetyTime
Parameter.Description: Maximum time in fast charge
Parameter.EngineeringNote: T_FAST_CHG 1:0 Sets the fast-charge safety timer, t FC . 0b00 = Timer disabled 0b01 = 3 hours 0b10 = 5 hours 0b11 = 7 hours

Parameter.name: ErTmiHotBatteryTemperatureThreshold
Parameter.Description: Battery temperature threhold to enter JEITA hot mode
Parameter.EngineeringNote: THM_HOT 7:6 Sets the V HOT JEITA Temperature Threshold 0b00 = V HOT = 0.411V (45ºC for β = 3380K) 0b01 = V HOT = 0.367V (50ºC for β = 3380K) 0b10 = V HOT = 0.327V (55ºC for β = 3380K) 0b11 = V HOT = 0.291V (60ºC for β = 3380K)

Parameter.name: ErTmiSuspendChargeCurrentDrawEnable
Parameter.Description: Enable suspension of current draw from charging adapter source
Parameter.EngineeringNote: USBS 1 Setting this bit places CHGIN in USB suspend mode. 0 = CHGIN is not suspended and can draw current from an adapter source. 1 = CHGIN is suspended and can not draw current from an adapter source. Note: USBS = 1 results in CHGIN_I interrupt AND CHGIN_DTLS[1:0] = 0b00.

Parameter.name: ErTmiTerminationCurrent
Parameter.Description: Charging terminates when charge current drops to this level
Parameter.EngineeringNote: I_TERM 4:3 Charger Termination Current (I TERM ). I_TERM[1:0] sets the charger termination current as a percentage of the fast-charge current I FAST-CHG . 00 = 5% 01 = 7.5% 10 = 10% 11 = 15%

Parameter.name: ErTmiWarmBatteryTemperatureThreshold
Parameter.Description: Battery temperature threhold to enter JEITA warm mode
Parameter.EngineeringNote: THM_WARM 5:4 Sets the V WARM JEITA Temperature Threshold 0b00 = V WARM = 0.511V (35ºC for β = 3380K) 0b01 = V WARM = 0.459V (40ºC for β = 3380K) 0b10 = V WARM = 0.411V (45ºC for β = 3380K) 0b11 = V WARM = 0.367V (50ºC for β = 3380K)

ParameterGroup.name: PowerManagementGlobalConfiguration
ParameterGroup.Description: Power management integrated circuit (PMIC) global configuration parameters

Parameter.name: ErTmiManualResetTime
Parameter.Description: Manual reset push button time for power management integrated circuit (PMIC)

ParameterGroup.name: PowerManagementOutputConfiguration
ParameterGroup.Description: Power management integrated circuit (PMIC) output configuration parameters

Parameter.name: ErTmiActiveDischargeEnable
Parameter.Description: Channel's active discharge enable to help the output voltage discharge
Parameter.EngineeringNote: ADE_SBBX/ADE_LDO 3 SIMO Buck-Boost Channel X/LDO Active-Discharge Enable 0 = The active discharge function is disabled. When SBBX/LDO is disabled, its discharge rate is a function of the output capacitance and the external load. 1 = The active discharge function is enabled. When SBBX /LDO is disabled, an internal resistor (R AD_SBBX/LDO ) is activated from SBBX /LDO to PGND to help the output voltage discharge. The output voltage discharge rate is a function of the output capacitance, the external loading, and the internal R AD_SBBX /LDO load. Index 0 = SBB0 Index 1 = SBB1 Index 2 = SBB2 Index 3 = LDO

Parameter.name: ErTmiDriveStrength
Parameter.Description: Buck-boost drive strength trim
Parameter.EngineeringNote: DRV_SBB 1:0 SIMO Buck-Boost (all channels) Drive Strength Trim. See the Drive Strength section for more details. 0b00 = Fastest transition time 0b01 = A little slower than 0b00 0b10 = A little slower than 0b01 0b11 = A little slower than 0b10

Parameter.name: ErTmiLowDropoutVoltage
Parameter.Description: Low-dropout nominal target output voltage
Parameter.EngineeringNote: TV_LDO 6:0 LDO Target Output Voltage This 7-bit configuration is a linear transfer function that starts at 0.5V, ends at 3.675V, with 25mV increments. 0x00 = 0.500V 0x01 = 0.525V 0x02 = 0.550V 0x03 = 0.575V 0x04 = 0.600V 0x05 = 0.625V 0x06 = 0.650V 0x07 = 0.675V 0x08 = 0.700V ... 0x7E = 3.650V 0x7F = 3.675V When TV_LDO[7] = 0, TV_LDO[6:0] sets the LDO's output voltage range from 0.5V to 3.675V. When TV_LDO[7] = 1, TV_LDO[6:0] sets the LDO's output voltage from 1.825V to 5V.

Parameter.name: ErTmiOperationMode
Parameter.Description: Channel's operation mode
Parameter.EngineeringNote: OP_MODE 6 Operation Mode of SBB0 X = Buck-boost mode 1 = Buck mode Index 0 = SBB0 Index 1 = SBB1 Index 2 = SBB2

Parameter.name: ErTmiPeakCurrentLimit
Parameter.Description: Channel's peak inductor current limit
Parameter.EngineeringNote: IP_SBBX 1:0 SIMO Buck-Boost Channel X Peak Current Limit 0b00 = 1.000A 0b01 = 0.750A 0b10 = 0.500A 0b11 = 0.333A Index 0 = SBB0 Index 1 = SBB1 Index 2 = SBB2

Parameter.name: ErTmiVoltage
Parameter.Description: Channel's nominal target output voltage
Parameter.EngineeringNote: TV_SBBX 6:0 SIMO Buck-Boost Channel X Target Output Voltage This 7-bit configuration is a piece-wise linear transfer function with 25mV increments from 0.5V to 1.675V and 50mV increments from 1.7V to 5.5V. 0x00 = 0.500V 0x01 = 0.525V 0x02 = 0.550V 0x03 = 0.575V 0x04 = 0.600V ... 0x30 = 1.700V 0x31 = 1.750V 0x32 = 1.800V ... 0x7B = 5.450V 0x7C = 5.500V 0x7D to 0x7F = Reserved Index 0 = SBB0 Index 1 = SBB1 Index 2 = SBB2

Parameter.name: ErTmiApcDisabledProximityDetectedThreshold
Parameter.Description: Threshold, when automatic pulse control (APC) is disabled, in which if proximity value is above, proximity is deemed. The two least significant bits are ignored as only the upper 8-bits are compared to the upper 8-bits of the 10-bit ADC data. Therefore, this is limited to multiples of 4.
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 7:0 PIHTL 0x00 RW This register contains the HIGH threshold which is an 8-bit value which is compared against the upper 8 bits of the 10-bit proximity value. If the value generated by the proximity ADC (PDATA) is above the PIHTL threshold and the PPERS value is reached, then the high proximity threshold is breached. With Automatic Pulse Control (APC) disabled, then the proximity data converts to a 10-bit value. PIHTL contains an 8-bit threshold which is compared against the upper 8 bits of the 10-bit value.

Parameter.name: ErTmiApcDisabledProximityNotDetectedThreshold
Parameter.Description: Threshold, when automatic pulse control (APC) is disabled, in which if proximity value is below, proximity is not deemed. The two least significant bits are ignored as only the upper 8-bits are compared to the upper 8-bits of the 10-bit ADC data. Therefore, this is limited to multiples of 4.
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 7:0 PILTL 0x00 RW This register contains the LOW threshold which is an 8-bit value which is compared against the upper 8 bits of the 10-bit proximity value. If the value generated by the proximity ADC (PDATA) is below the PILTL threshold and the PPERS value is reached, then the low proximity threshold is breached. With Automatic Pulse Control (APC) disabled, then the proximity data converts to a 10-bit value. PILTL contains an 8-bit threshold which is compared against the upper 8 bits of the 10-bit value.

Parameter.name: ErTmiApcEnabledProximityDetectedThreshold
Parameter.Description: Threshold, when automatic pulse control (APC) is enabled, in which if proximity value is above, proximity is deemed
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 7:0 PIHTL 0x00 RW This register contains the low byte of the 14-bit proximity HIGH threshold 5:0 PIHTH 0x00 RW This register contains the upper 6 bits of the 14-bit proximity HIGH threshold The contents of the PIHTH and PIHTL registers are combined and treated as a fourteen (14) bit threshold high value. If the value generated by the proximity ADC (PDATA) is above the PIHTL/H threshold and the PPERS value is reached, then the high proximity threshold is breached.

Parameter.name: ErTmiApcEnabledProximityNotDetectedThreshold
Parameter.Description: Threshold, when automatic pulse control (APC) is enabled, in which if proximity value is below, proximity is not deemed
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 7:0 PILTL 0x00 RW This register contains the low byte of the 14-bit proximity LOW threshold 5:0 PILTH 0x00 RW This register contains the upper 6 bits of the 14-bit proximity LOW threshold The contents of the PILTH and PILTL registers are combined and treated as a fourteen (14) bit threshold low value. If the value generated by the proximity ADC (PDATA) is below the PILTL/H threshold and the PPERS value is reached, then the low proximity threshold is breached.

Parameter.name: ErTmiAutomaticPulseControlDisable
Parameter.Description: Proximity sensor automatic pulse control (APC) disable

Parameter.name: ErTmiDriveStrengthCurrent
Parameter.Description: Drive strength of the infrared vertical cavity surface emitting laser current
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 3:0 PLDRIVE 0 (0000) RW This field sets the drive strength of the IR VCSEL current. Values are approximate; actual current through VCSEL is factory trimmed to normalize IR intensity. For lowest part to part variation, 7mA is recommended. Value VCSEL Current 5 (0101) 7mA 6 (0110) 8mA 7 (0111) 9mA 8 (1000) 10mA All other values Reserved

Parameter.name: ErTmiInfraredSensorGain
Parameter.Description: Proximity IR (infrared) sensor gain
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 7:6 PGAIN 2 (10) RW This field sets the gain of the proximity IR sensor. Value Gain 0 (00) 1x 1 (01) 2x 2 (10) 4x 3 (11) 8x

Parameter.name: ErTmiOffEarHysteresis
Parameter.Description: Hysteresis time preventing a quick transition when off ear is detected

Parameter.name: ErTmiOnEarHysteresis
Parameter.Description: Hysteresis time preventing a quick transition when on ear is detected

Parameter.name: ErTmiPersistenceFilter
Parameter.Description: Compared to the number of consecutive proximity results outside of the threshold limits to determine if proximity interrupt is asserted
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 3:0 PPERS 0 (0000) RW This register sets the proximity persistence filter. Value Interrupt 0 (0000) Every proximity cycle 1 (0001) Any value outside proximity thresholds 2 (0010) 2 consecutive proximity values out of range 3 (0011) 3 consecutive proximity values out of range ... ... 15 (1111) 15 consecutive proximity values out of range The frequency of consecutive proximity channel results outside of threshold limits are counted; this count value is compared against the PPERS value. If the counter is equal to the PPERS value an interrupt is asserted. Any time a proximity channel result is inside the threshold values the counter is cleared.

Parameter.name: ErTmiPhotodiode
Parameter.Description: Photodiode selection
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 1:0 PDSELECT 10 RW Proximity photodiode selection Value Photodiode Selected 00 No photodiode 01 Far photodiode 10 Near photodiode (default) 11 Both photodiodes

Parameter.name: ErTmiProximityDataOffset
Parameter.Description: Proximity data offset adjustment
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 7:0 POFFSETL 0x00 RW This register contains the magnitude portion of proximity offset adjust value. 0 POFFSETH 0 RW This register contains the sign portion of proximity offset adjust value. Typically, optical and/or electrical crosstalk negatively influence proximity operation and results. The POFFSETL/POFFSETH registers provide a mechanism to remove system crosstalk from the proximity data. POFFSETL and POFFSETH contains the magnitude and sign of a value which adjusts PDATA is generated in the AFE. An offset value in the range of ± 255 is possible.

Parameter.name: ErTmiProximityEnable
Parameter.Description: Enable the proximity sensor

Parameter.name: ErTmiPulseLength
Parameter.Description: Length of time of proximity pulse
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 7:5 PPULSE_ LEN 3 (011) RW Proximity pulse length. Value Pulse Length 0 (000) 1μs 1 (001) 2μs 2 (010) 4μs 3 (011) 8μs 4 (100) 12μs 5 (101) 16μs 6 (110) 24μs 7 (111) 32μs The PPULSE_LEN field sets the length (width) of all IR VCSEL pulses within the proximity cycle. Longer pulses result in increased proximity range and typically result in less electrical noise generated in the analog front end.

Parameter.name: ErTmiPulsesPerCycle
Parameter.Description: Maximum number of pulses in a single proximity cycle
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 5:0 PPULSE 15 (001111) RW Maximum number of pulses in a single proximity cycle. Value Maximum Number of Pulses 0 (00000) 1 1 (00001) 2 2 (00010) 3 ... ... 63 (11111) 64 The PPULSE field sets the maximum number of IR VCSEL pulses that may occur in a proximity cycle. The proximity engine will automatically continue to add IR VCSEL pulses, up to the value set in PPULSE or if a near-saturation condition occurs if Automatic Pulse Control (APC) is enabled. The dynamic range of the sensor is automatically adjusted to detect distant targets as well as prevent saturation from close targets. This operation also reduces power consumption because proximity integration period is automatically shortened when a target is close to the sensor. If Automatic Pulse Control (APC) is disabled by setting bit 6 in CFG6 to 1, then PPULSE always determines the number of proximity pulses to be transmitted.

Parameter.name: ErTmiSamplePeriod
Parameter.Description: Time between each proximity sample

Parameter.name: ErTmiProximityAdcData
Parameter.Description: Proximity sensor ADC data
Parameter.EngineeringNote: 7:0 PDATAL 0x00 RO This register contains the low byte of the 14-bit proximity ADC data when APC is enabled. If APC is disabled, this register contains the upper 8 most significant bits of the 10-bit proximity value. 7:0 PDATAH 0x00 RO This register contains the high byte of the 14-bit proximity ADC data when APC is enabled. If APC is disabled, bits 1:0 contain the lower 2 bits of the 10-bit proximity value. Proximity data is stored as a 14-bit value (two bytes). Reading the low byte first latches the high byte. Proximity detection uses an Automatic Pulse Control (APC) mechanism that adjusts the number of pulses per measurement based on the magnitude of the reflected IR signal. As the magnitude of the signal increases, the number of pulses decreases. Proximity detection uses a 10-bit ADC that is extended to a 14-bit dynamic range for PDATA using the following formula: PDATA = ADC value x (16 / actual number of pulses transmitted) PDATA is therefore proportional to the reflected energy independent of the number of pulses transmitted. If Automatic Pulse Control (APC) is disabled by setting bit 6 in CFG6 to 1, then the proximity data converts to a 10-bit value. PDATAL contains the 8 most significant bits of the 10-bit value and PDATAH bit locations 1:0 contain the lower 2 bits. When APC is disabled, only the upper 8 bits are compared against the threshold values contained in PILTL and PIHTL.

Parameter.name: ToneLevelOffset
Parameter.Description: Tone level offset applied to tone level relative to indicator's base tone level, where level is attenuation relative to full scale and therefore negative offset means louder
Parameter.EngineeringNote: This parameter provides an offset in dB to the final tone level. The base tone level is in units of -dBFS and so the final tone level in units of -dBFS is the value of the ToneLevel parameter defined in the IndicatorParameters plus this offset. For example: ToneLevel = 18 (-dBFS) ToneLevelOffset = -6 (dB) Final tone level = 18-6 = 12 (-dBFS) In other words, the tone went from 18dB below full scale to 12dB below full scale (it got louder).
